text: Cluster operators inspect account, partition, memory, and accelerator requirements before submission.
A batch allocation reserves eight A100 devices on one node for two isolated client groups.
Client two maps its four distributed ranks to visible accelerator indices four through seven.
The production server and clients communicate through provisioned TLS rather than a simulator thread.
Node-local scratch holds ephemeral service kits while durable evidence is written to project storage.
Offline containers and environments avoid package installation during monitored accelerator time.
A data copier node is appropriate for staging large immutable checkpoints outside compute allocations.
Scheduler commands are issued sparingly to respect controller remote procedure call rate limits.
The job records its hostname and scheduler identifier so artifacts can be traced to an allocation.
A clean branch and pinned release marker prevent an obsolete qualification script from running.
Every expected file is checked before the job starts any process on an allocated accelerator.
The model revision file must match the exact staged Hugging Face snapshot used by all participants.
A short smaller-model gate exercises the same trainable-state bridge before loading the target model.
The target phase starts only after the gate completes aggregation, persistence, and reload checks.
Service logs are filtered by job identifier so sequential production jobs cannot mix evidence.
The watcher captures checkpoint metadata before ephemeral production workspaces are removed.
Checkpoint inspection waits for a nonempty stable file after the server reports completed persistence.
A failure artifact retains collected server and client logs for diagnosis without rerunning immediately.
Signals trigger controlled cleanup and return a nonzero status rather than disguising an interrupted run.
The requested wall time includes startup and bounded recovery while actual completion releases resources early.
GPU samples must cover every allocated index and identify the expected A100 SXM model.
Peak host memory and accelerator memory are interpreted separately during capacity review.
Trainable-only payloads reduce network and persistence traffic while retaining full local computation.
The immutable base checkpoint is never averaged because both sites already hold the identical revision.
Only selected decoder-layer weights are initialized on the server for FedAvg aggregation.
The server frees temporary full-model objects before client worker groups begin loading their copies.
Four local examples per rank provide sixteen distinct records at each client during every round.
Three rounds consume forty-eight ordered examples from each fixed client partition.
Input state hashes prove both clients started a round from the same global parameters.
Different output hashes prove the two local partitions did not return identical client updates.
Persisted hashes link a completed server round to the inputs received in the next round.
Sampled tensor coordinates provide a direct numerical check of equal-weight federated averaging.
Payload limits reject an accidental fallback from selected-state exchange to a full checkpoint.
The final checkpoint contains no frozen keys and reloads with the expected tensor count and shapes.
Loss values and parameter changes must remain finite on all distributed workers.
The client reports every local loss step so a successful round is not represented by one scalar alone.
Equal client weights are explicit and verified instead of inferred from scheduler placement.
Aggregation and persistence markers must appear once for each configured federated round.
The evidence summary reports total logical model traffic alongside elapsed allocation time.
A resource review can compare training work with orchestration, transfer, and checkpoint overhead.
The experiment does not claim convergence from a small deterministic qualification corpus.
A later study may replace these records with approved site-owned data using the same state contract.
The current qualification focuses on federated correctness rather than downstream task accuracy.
All configuration values written into job folders are nonsecret paths, hashes, and public revisions.
The runbook gives explicit commands for preflight, submission, monitoring, and artifact inspection.
No additional accelerator run is authorized until the new code and generated job are locally validated.
A failed gate stops the workflow before the fourteen billion parameter target phase begins.
A successful target captures three-round continuity, FedAvg samples, final persistence, and reload evidence.
